newsitem.title: SENEGAL: US army starts training of Senegalese peacekeepers.
newsitem.headline: US army starts training of Senegalese peacekeepers.

text.p: Sixty U.S. soldiers began peacekeeping training for 750 Senegalese troops on Thursday as part of a wider African initiative.

"These trainings are aimed at building capacities to mount an effective, collective response to humanitarian and other crises on the African continent," warrant officer Robert Hart told Reuters at the start of the course in Thies, near Dakar.
The American trainers arrived in the West African country last month from the Third Special Forces Group (Airborne), Fort Bragg, North Carolina.
A similar 60-day multi-function programme is running simultaneously in the east African state of Uganda under Washington's African Crisis Reponse Initiative (ACRI).

"The end result will be a battalion-size unit from both Senegal and Uganda, which will be capable of conducting effective peacekeeping or humnitarian assistance operations when directed by their sovereign leaders," a U.S. statement said.

U.S. officials say ACRI's objective is not the creation of a standing African force. The emphasis is on the provision of training and a limited amount of equipment, primarily communication gear, to enhance peacekeeping capability in a multinational context.
A similar course is planned for Malawi next month.

Senegal has participated in several peacekeeping missions notably in Lebanon, Liberia, and Rwanda. Its soldiers are among U.N. troops monitoring the Kuwait-Iraq border since the end of the Gulf war. A Senegalese general has been named to head a planned peacekeeping force for troubled Congo-Brazzaville.
U.S. officials say ACRI is line with a call by the Group of Eight industrial nations at their Denver summit for support for long-term efforts to promote African peacekeeping capacities.
